course.title: SQL Masterclass
course.tagline: Zero to advanced, one module at a time.
course.standard: PostgreSQL-first, with MySQL, SQLite and SQL Server notes.
course.description: Module 08 teaches ORDER BY, ASC/DESC, multi-key sorting, NULL placement, LIMIT, OFFSET, stable pagination and the performance cost of sorting.
outcomes: Sort by one or many keys

modules.title: ORDER BY, LIMIT and OFFSET
modules.goal: Produce deterministic sorted pages and top-N reports.

topics.title: Introduction to ORDER BY
topics.simple: ORDER BY result rows ko sort karta hai.
topics.pro: ORDER BY sorts the final result set using one or more sort expressions; it runs after SELECT and DISTINCT and before LIMIT.
points: No ORDER BY means no guaranteed order.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC;

topics.title: Sorting Rows
topics.simple: Sorting se rows ek predictable sequence me aate hain.
topics.pro: A sort key defines the comparison used to order rows; equal keys keep an unspecified relative order unless a tie-breaker is added.
points: One key is enough for simple reports.
The result is only guaranteed when the order is total.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks;

topics.title: ASC
topics.simple: ASC ascending order me sort karta hai — chhota se bada.
topics.pro: ASC is the default sort direction and orders values from smallest to largest, or A to Z for text.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks ASC;

topics.title: DESC
topics.simple: DESC descending order me sort karta hai — bada se chhota.
topics.pro: DESC orders values from largest to smallest, or Z to A for text.
points: It is not a stable sort by itself.
Add a tie-breaker for deterministic pages.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC;

topics.title: Sorting Numeric Data
topics.simple: Numbers natural numeric order me sort hote hain, text order me nahi.
topics.pro: Numeric columns sort by value, so 9 comes before 10; storing numbers as text would sort 10 before 9.
points: Use numeric types for numeric sorting.
Casting text to numeric changes the order.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC;

topics.title: Sorting Text Data
topics.simple: Text sort collation par depend karta hai; case aur language order badal sakta hai.
topics.pro: Text ordering follows the column collation, which controls case and locale rules; use LOWER() or a case-insensitive collation when needed.
points: A and a may sort differently by collation.

example.sql: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY LOWER(name);

topics.title: Sorting Date Values
topics.simple: Dates chronological order me sort hoti hain.
topics.pro: Date and timestamp values sort chronologically; DESC gives newest first.
points: Earlier dates come first in ASC.
Timestamps include time within the day.

example.sql: SELECT student_id, enrolled_on FROM enrollments ORDER BY enrolled_on DESC;

topics.title: Multiple Sort Keys
topics.simple: Pehla key main order deta hai, doosra key ties todta hai.
topics.pro: Multiple ORDER BY expressions are applied left to right: the first is primary, later keys break ties.
points: Each key has its own direction.
The last key should make the order deterministic.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST, name ASC;
example.output: Highest known marks first, ties alphabetical.

topics.title: Sorting by Aliases and Expressions
topics.simple: ORDER BY alias ya expression use kar sakta hai.
topics.pro: ORDER BY can reference a select-list alias or repeat an expression, because it is evaluated after SELECT.
points: Aliases do not work in WHERE.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks * 2 AS doubled FROM students ORDER BY doubled DESC;
example.output: Rows ordered by the doubled value.

topics.title: NULL Sorting
topics.simple: PostgreSQL me ASC default NULLs last, DESC default NULLs first.
topics.pro: By default PostgreSQL treats NULL as larger than any non-null value: ASC places NULLs last and DESC places them first; NULLS FIRST/LAST overrides it.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks ASC NULLS LAST;
example.output: Known marks ascending, NULL marks last.

topics.title: LIMIT
topics.simple: LIMIT result ki maximum row count set karta hai.
topics.pro: LIMIT caps the number of rows returned after sorting; LIMIT without ORDER BY returns an arbitrary subset.
points: Use ORDER BY for meaningful top-N.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 3;

topics.title: OFFSET
topics.simple: OFFSET starting rows skip karta hai.
topics.pro: OFFSET skips a number of rows after sorting and before the limit is applied.
points: Large offsets still scan skipped rows.
Use with ORDER BY for stable pages.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3;

topics.title: Pagination
topics.simple: Pagination me page size aur page number se LIMIT/OFFSET nikalte hain.
topics.pro: A page uses LIMIT page_size OFFSET (page - 1) * page_size, with a deterministic ORDER BY so rows do not shift between pages.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20;

topics.title: Top N Records
topics.simple: Top N ke liye ORDER BY DESC aur LIMIT N use karo.
topics.pro: Top-N queries sort by the ranking key descending and cap the result; ties need an explicit tie-breaker or a window function for exact semantics.
points: Ties can make the cut arbitrary.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5;

topics.title: Bottom N Records
topics.simple: Bottom N ke liye ascending order aur LIMIT use karo.
topics.pro: Bottom-N queries sort ascending and cap the result; NULL placement can affect what counts as the bottom.
points: NULLS LAST keeps unknown values out of the bottom.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5;

topics.title: Deterministic Ordering
topics.simple: Deterministic order ke liye unique tie-breaker add karo.
topics.pro: A total ordering uses a unique key as the final sort expression, so equal values cannot swap between pages or runs.
points: Add id as the last key.
Without it, LIMIT can change between runs.
Stable pages need a total order.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC;
example.output: Marks descending, NULLs last, id breaking every tie.

topics.title: Positional ORDER BY
topics.simple: ORDER BY 2 select list ke doosre column ko refer karta hai.
topics.pro: ORDER BY can use a select-list position, but positional references are fragile when the projection changes and should be avoided in application SQL.
points: Position 1 is the first output column.
It breaks when columns are reordered.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY 2 DESC;
example.output: Rows ordered by marks, the second column.

topics.title: ORDER BY with WHERE
topics.simple: WHERE pehle filter karta hai, phir ORDER BY sort karta hai.
topics.pro: Logical evaluation filters rows in WHERE, projects them in SELECT, then sorts the surviving rows in ORDER BY.
points: Sorting only the filtered rows is cheaper.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks >= 60 ORDER BY marks DESC;

topics.title: Sorting Performance
topics.simple: Bade result ko sort karna costly hota hai; index madad kar sakta hai.
topics.pro: A sort may use memory or disk; a matching B-tree index can return rows already ordered and avoid a sort for prefix-ordered queries.
points: Indexes help matching ORDER BY prefixes.

example.sql: EXPLAIN SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
example.output: An Index Scan or a Sort depending on available indexes.

topics.title: Practical Ranking Report
topics.simple: Ab filter, sort, tie-breaker aur limit mila kar ranking report banao.
topics.pro: A reliable ranking report combines a filter, a deterministic ORDER BY, an explicit NULL policy and a LIMIT, and is reviewed with EXPLAIN when it grows.

example.sql: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks IS NOT NULL ORDER BY marks DESC, id ASC LIMIT 10;
example.output: Top ten known marks with stable ties.

learn.q: What does ORDER BY do?
learn.why: ORDER BY defines the final row order.

learn.q: Which direction is the default?
learn.why: ASC is assumed when no direction is written.

learn.q: What does DESC do?
learn.why: DESC reverses the comparison order.

learn.q: How do you sort by marks highest first?
learn.why: DESC puts the largest values first.

learn.q: How do you break ties after marks?
options: Add name ASC as a second key
learn.answer: Add name ASC as a second key
learn.why: Later sort keys break ties from earlier keys.

learn.q: Can ORDER BY use a select-list alias?
learn.why: ORDER BY is evaluated after SELECT, so aliases exist.

learn.q: Does PostgreSQL put NULLs first or last for ASC?
learn.why: NULL sorts as larger than non-null values, so ASC puts it last.

learn.q: Does PostgreSQL put NULLs first or last for DESC?
learn.why: DESC reverses the default, so NULLs come first.

learn.q: Which clause overrides NULL placement?
learn.why: Both are ORDER BY modifiers.

learn.q: What does LIMIT 5 return?
learn.why: The result can have fewer rows.

learn.q: What does OFFSET 10 do?
learn.why: OFFSET drops rows before the limit is applied.

learn.q: What is page 3 with page size 10?
learn.why: Offset is (page - 1) × size.

learn.q: What is the top-N pattern?
options: ORDER BY key DESC LIMIT N
ORDER BY key ASC LIMIT N
learn.answer: ORDER BY key DESC LIMIT N
learn.why: Sort the ranking key descending, then cap.

learn.q: What is the bottom-N pattern?
options: ORDER BY key ASC LIMIT N
ORDER BY key DESC LIMIT N
learn.answer: ORDER BY key ASC LIMIT N
learn.why: Ascending puts the smallest first.

learn.q: Why add a unique tie-breaker?
learn.why: A total order prevents equal keys from swapping.

learn.q: What does ORDER BY 2 refer to?
learn.why: Positional ORDER BY references the select list.

learn.q: Should application SQL use positional ORDER BY?
learn.why: Changing the projection can silently change the sort.

learn.q: Does WHERE run before ORDER BY?
learn.why: Rows are filtered before they are sorted.

learn.q: What does LIMIT without ORDER BY return?
options: The first rows by primary key
learn.why: Without ORDER BY there is no guaranteed row order.

learn.q: Which clause applies last?
learn.why: Logical order ends with LIMIT/OFFSET.

interview.q: What is ORDER BY?
interview.answer: The clause that sorts the final result set using one or more expressions.

interview.q: What is the default sort direction?
interview.answer: ASC, from smallest to largest or A to Z.

interview.q: How do you sort descending?
interview.answer: Add DESC after the sort expression.

interview.q: How do multiple ORDER BY keys work?
interview.answer: They are applied left to right; later keys break ties from earlier keys.

interview.q: Can ORDER BY use an alias?
interview.answer: Yes, because ORDER BY is evaluated after SELECT.

interview.q: Can WHERE use a SELECT alias?
interview.answer: No, because WHERE runs before SELECT.

interview.q: How does PostgreSQL sort NULLs by default?
interview.answer: As larger than non-null values: NULLS LAST for ASC and NULLS FIRST for DESC.

interview.q: How do you force NULLs last?
interview.answer: Add NULLS LAST to the ORDER BY expression.

interview.q: What does LIMIT do?
interview.answer: Caps the number of rows returned after sorting.

interview.q: What does OFFSET do?
interview.answer: Skips a number of rows before the limit is applied.

interview.q: How do you calculate a pagination offset?
interview.answer: Offset = (page - 1) × page_size, with page 1 at offset 0.

interview.q: Why is LIMIT without ORDER BY unsafe?
interview.answer: The database may return any subset because no row order is guaranteed.

interview.q: Why is a tie-breaker important for pagination?
interview.answer: Equal sort keys can swap between pages; a unique final key makes the order total.

interview.q: What is top-N SQL?
interview.answer: ORDER BY ranking_key DESC LIMIT n, with a tie-breaker for stable results.

interview.q: What is the difference between LIMIT and FETCH FIRST?
interview.answer: LIMIT is PostgreSQL/MySQL/SQLite syntax; FETCH FIRST is standard SQL and also supported by PostgreSQL.

interview.q: Why can a large OFFSET be slow?
interview.answer: The database still has to scan and discard the skipped rows.

interview.q: What is keyset pagination?
interview.answer: Paginating by a stable key, such as WHERE id > last_id ORDER BY id LIMIT n, instead of skipping a large offset.

interview.q: How can an index help ORDER BY?
interview.answer: A B-tree index matching the sort prefix can return rows already ordered and avoid a sort.

interview.q: Why does text sort vary?
interview.answer: Text ordering follows the collation, which controls case and locale rules.

interview.q: Can ORDER BY use an expression?
interview.answer: Yes, including functions and arithmetic, but the expression must be evaluated for each row.

labs.title: Sort marks ascending
labs.task: Return name and marks lowest first.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks ASC;

labs.title: Sort marks descending
labs.task: Return name and marks highest first.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC;

labs.title: Sort names
labs.task: Return names alphabetically.
labs.solution: SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY name ASC;
labs.expected: A to Z under the collation.

labs.title: Sort dates
labs.task: Return enrollments newest first.
labs.solution: SELECT student_id, enrolled_on FROM enrollments ORDER BY enrolled_on DESC;

labs.title: Multiple keys
labs.task: Sort by marks descending, then name ascending.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC, name ASC;

labs.title: Sort by alias
labs.task: Return name and marks doubled, ordered by doubled descending.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks * 2 AS doubled FROM students ORDER BY doubled DESC;

labs.title: Sort by expression
labs.task: Order by marks plus 5 descending.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks + 5 AS boosted FROM students ORDER BY boosted DESC;

labs.title: NULLs last
labs.task: Sort marks ascending with NULLs last.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks ASC NULLS LAST;

labs.title: NULLs first
labs.task: Sort marks descending with NULLs last.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST;

labs.title: Limit three
labs.task: Return the top three by marks.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC LIMIT 3;

labs.title: Offset three
labs.task: Skip the top three and return the next three.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC LIMIT 3 OFFSET 3;

labs.title: Page three
labs.task: Return page 3 with page size 10.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC LIMIT 10 OFFSET 20;

labs.title: Top five
labs.task: Return the five highest marks.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC LIMIT 5;

labs.title: Bottom five
labs.task: Return the five lowest known marks.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks ASC NULLS LAST LIMIT 5;

labs.title: Deterministic ties
labs.task: Sort by marks descending with id as the tie-breaker.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST, id ASC;

labs.title: Positional order
labs.task: Order by the second output column descending.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY 2 DESC NULLS LAST;

labs.title: Filter then sort
labs.task: Return students above 60, highest first.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks > 60 ORDER BY marks DESC;

labs.title: Check the plan
labs.task: Explain the top-ten marks query.
labs.solution: EXPLAIN SELECT name FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST LIMIT 10;
labs.expected: A plan with an index scan or sort.

labs.title: Standard fetch
labs.task: Return the top three using FETCH FIRST.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students ORDER BY marks DESC NULLS LAST FETCH FIRST 3 ROWS ONLY;

labs.title: Ranking report
labs.task: Return the top ten known marks with stable ties.
labs.solution: SELECT name, marks FROM students WHERE marks IS NOT NULL ORDER BY marks DESC, id ASC LIMIT 10;
labs.expected: Top ten known marks, ties by id.

logic.q: Why is ORDER BY without LIMIT potentially expensive?
logic.answer: The database may sort the entire result before returning any rows.

logic.q: Why is LIMIT without ORDER BY arbitrary?
logic.answer: There is no guaranteed row order, so any subset may be chosen.
Equal sort keys can swap between runs and pages; a unique final key makes the order total.

logic.q: Why does ASC put NULLs last in PostgreSQL?
logic.answer: NULL sorts as larger than any non-null value in the default ordering.

logic.q: Why does DESC put NULLs first?
logic.answer: DESC reverses the default ordering, so the largest value (NULL) comes first.

logic.q: Why can text sorting surprise you?
logic.answer: Collation controls case and locale rules, so A and a may not sort as expected.

logic.q: Why does a large OFFSET get slower?
logic.answer: The server still scans and discards every skipped row.

logic.q: Why is keyset pagination often faster?
logic.answer: It seeks directly after the last key instead of counting and discarding rows.

logic.q: Why does an alias work in ORDER BY but not WHERE?
logic.answer: ORDER BY runs after SELECT defines the alias; WHERE runs before it.

logic.q: Why is positional ORDER BY fragile?
logic.answer: Changing the select list reorders or removes the referenced position.

logic.q: Why does WHERE run before ORDER BY?
logic.answer: Filtering first reduces the rows that must be sorted.

logic.q: Why does SELECT DISTINCT restrict ORDER BY expressions?
logic.answer: For DISTINCT, ORDER BY expressions must appear in the select list so the sort is defined on the projected rows.

logic.q: Why can an index satisfy ORDER BY?
logic.answer: A B-tree index matching the sort prefix returns rows in the requested order without a separate sort.

logic.q: Why does LIMIT apply after ORDER BY?
logic.answer: The rows must be ordered before the first N can be chosen.

logic.q: Why is ORDER BY random() expensive?
logic.answer: It computes a random value for every row and sorts the whole set with no useful index.

revision.answer: Left to right; later keys break ties.

revision.q: Where does PostgreSQL put NULLs in ASC?
Where does PostgreSQL put NULLs in DESC?

revision.answer: Caps the number of rows returned.
